modes.cue_notes: Lie flat on the back with legs extended and slightly apart, arms alongside the body with palms facing up. Eyes closed. Allow every muscle to release completely. Breathe naturally. The body integrates all preceding postures. Remain completely still unless there is physical discomfort.

source: Traditional yin yoga; see Paul Grilley, Bernie Clark, Sarah Powers
notes: Final integration pose. All meridians are listed as Savasana integrates the entire practice. Typically held 5–15 minutes at the end of a session.

breathing_cues.entering: As you lower onto the floor, exhale completely and let the breath settle into its natural rhythm without manipulation.
breathing_cues.holding: Allow the breath to become effortless and involuntary. Notice the belly softening on each inhale, the chest widening, and the whole body gently sinking heavier on each exhale. No controlling — just observing.
breathing_cues.exiting: Before moving, take one slow, deliberate inhale and let the exhale carry you into gentle awareness of your fingertips and toes.

modifications.name: Blanket under knees
modifications.description: Place a folded blanket or bolster under the knees to reduce lumbar strain. Especially helpful for students with lower back tension or lordosis.

modifications.name: Bolster under knees
modifications.description: Use a full bolster under the knees for a more elevated support that completely releases the psoas and lumbar region.

modifications.name: Eye pillow
modifications.description: Place a lightly weighted eye pillow over the eyes to promote sensory withdrawal (pratyahara) and deepen the parasympathetic response.

modifications.name: Blanket roll under cervical spine
modifications.description: Roll a small blanket and place it under the neck curve to support students with cervical lordosis or neck discomfort.

emotional_release_potential.notes: Surrendering to stillness can surface deep fear of dissolution or loss of control. The kidney-bladder axis governs primal fear; holding space for whatever arises in Savasana is essential teacher awareness.
Chronic sympathetic activation may make stillness uncomfortable initially. Students may experience a brief restless window before the nervous system fully downshifts.
Full-body release can open grief held in the chest and intercostals. Lung governs letting go; Savasana is the ultimate practice of non-attachment.
